rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding passage gradually teaches that people acquire their own deeds by choice and bear their own account.
rows.anchor: تدريجا في التبيان للناس بأن أعمالهم من كسبهم واختيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly-minded group wants only this life, serving its desires because it sees no life after death.
rows.anchor: قسم لم يرد إلا الدنيا فكانت أعماله لمرضاة شهواته معتقدا أن الدنيا هي قصارى مراتع النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife-minded group knows true success lies beyond this life, follows divinely guided works through the messengers, and is rewarded according to its aspiration.
rows.anchor: وقسم علم أن الفوز الحق هو فيما بعد هذه الحياة فعمل للآخرة مقتفيا ما هداه الله إليه من الأعمال بواسطة رسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between the two sentences supplies an added, contextual restriction: the first person wants the immediate world alone.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يريد إلا العاجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ājilah is an adjective whose omitted noun is life, understood from context and parallel wording.
rows.anchor: صفة موصوف محذوف يعلم من السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense depicts renewed worldly desire, while the past tense and omitted kāna make afterlife desire sound settled and especially worthy.
rows.anchor: والاختلاف بين جملة من كان يريد العاجلة } وجملة { ومن أراد الآخرة } بجعل الفعل مضارعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy literally means walking rather than running; here it denotes good works that lead to the afterlife as a traveler reaches a destination.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة السعي المشي دون العدو ، فسعي الآخرة هو الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive construction is a verbal noun related semantically to its object, and saʿy is an absolute object specifying kind.
rows.anchor: وإضافته إلى ضمير الآخرة من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله في المعنى ، أي السعي لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wanting the afterlife without striving is self-deception; any aim needs the actions that bring it about.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه على أن إرادة خير الآخرة من غير سعي غرور

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak’s poem rebukes hoping for salvation without following its path, like expecting a ship to sail on dry land.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن المبارك : ترجو النجاة ولم تسلك مسالكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial clause is nominal to signal stable, enduring faith; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares this to the wording about persevering believers.
rows.anchor: اسمية لدلالتها على الثبات والدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points out that people described as seeking the afterlife merit the announced reward.
rows.anchor: للتنبيه على أن المشار إليهم جديرون بما سيخبر به عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the effort thanked is a rational metaphor: the worker is approved, and describing the work conveys approval of its doer.
rows.anchor: والسعي المشكور هو المشكور ساعيه ، فوصفه به مجاز عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna indicates that the effort was already worthy of thanks in worldly life, while obedience also brings later reward.
rows.anchor: والتعبير ب { كان } في { كان سعيهم مشكورا } للدلالة على أن الوصف تحقق فيه من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse concludes the contrast in 17:18 and teaches that God gives worldly blessings even to disbelievers, while believers receive good in both worlds.
rows.anchor: تذييل لآية { من كان يريد العاجلة إلى آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s universal mercy includes disbelievers and accords with the verse about mercy encompassing everything and a divine saying that mercy preceded wrath.
rows.anchor: ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء ( الأعراف : 156 ) وقوله فيما رواه عنه نبيه إن رحمتي سبقت غضبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative tanwīn in kullan compensates for an omitted genitive, meaning both groups, and makes the word the object of numiddu.
rows.anchor: وتنوين كلا } تنوين عوض عن المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāʾulāʾi and hāʾulāʾi are a detailed apposition to the summary kull, identifying the two groups.
rows.anchor: بدل مفصل من مجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired apposition marvels at the breadth of God’s generosity.
rows.anchor: من سعة رحمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s instruction to follow Abū Bakr and ʿUmar illustrates how a coordinated pair can together form the apposition.
rows.anchor: كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اقتدوا باللذين من بعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet al-Mutalammis uses paired demonstratives to show the usual reference from the first demonstrative to the first item and the second to the second.
rows.anchor: ولا يقيم على ضيم يراد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imdād means a continuing succession of gifts, each new grant extending what came before.
rows.anchor: والإمداد : استرسال العطاء وتعاقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause is parenthetic or a conclusion: divine giving is not wholly withheld, and every creature has a share.
rows.anchor: وعطاء ربك جنس العطاء ، والمحظور : الممنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because both groups receive worldly gifts and people can observe differences, the Prophet is asked to reflect; the afterlife’s gifts for believers are greater.
rows.anchor: لما كان العطاء المبذول للفريقين هو عطاء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to look addresses the Prophet to raise his knowledge and also directs others to draw the lesson.
rows.anchor: والأمر بالنظر موجه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ترفيعا في درجات علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazar shifts from literal sight to repeated, reflective observation and can mean reasoning that yields knowledge or probability, as it does here.
rows.anchor: وقد شاع في كلام العرب استعماله في النظر المصحوب بالتدبر وتكرير مشاهدة أشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa is an interrogative used to alert the listener and syntactically suspends unẓur from taking its two objects.
rows.anchor: و ( كيف ) اسم استفهام مستعمل في التنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison concerns worldly provision, which reflection can observe, and prepares the contrast with the greater afterlife.
rows.anchor: والمراد التفضيل في عطاء الدنيا ، لأنه الذي يدركه التأمل والنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly rank is not tied to righteous conduct: Muslims and disbelievers, including people within each group, can surpass one another.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا التنظير التنبيه إلى أن عطاء الدنيا غير منوط بصلاح الأعمال ؛ ألا ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The differing worldly allotments arise from causes other than righteous deeds or the qualities of virtuous souls.
rows.anchor: مناط عطاء الدنيا أسباب ليست من وادي العمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences of darajāt and tafḍīlan are accusative specification; degrees metaphorically mean honor, and tafḍīl means extra blessing.
rows.anchor: ونصب { درجات } و { تفضيلا } على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife’s favor is a greater blessing than worldly blessings; a hadith illustrates the sense of surplus wealth.
rows.anchor: والدرجات مستعارة لعظمة الشرف ، والتفضيل : إعطاء الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Renouncing association with God is the basis of success and the first step toward good works, since shirk corrupts thought and reason.
rows.anchor: فإن خلاصة أسباب الفوز ترك الشرك لأن ذلك هو مبدأ الإقبال على العمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet receives the address as a continuation of the previous one, while its intended audience includes others, especially polytheists.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبيء تبع لخطاب قوله : انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqʿud metaphorically means remaining; the prohibition indirectly warns polytheists who already live in blame and abandonment that they will remain so if they persist.
rows.anchor: وتقعد } مستعار لمعنى المكث والدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolater is blamed by rational people and by God through revelation; worshipping stone or wood is deeply absurd.
rows.anchor: فأما ذمه فمن ذوي العقول ، إذ أعظم سخرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An idol cannot help its worshipper, and God abandons those who do not take Him as protector; the cited verses explain the lack of support.
rows.anchor: وأما خذلانه فلأنه اتخذ لنفسه وليا لا يغني عنه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a poem presenting Muhammad’s testament as including worship of God, care for kin and captives, and kindness to vulnerable people.
rows.anchor: أجدك لم تسمع وصاة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening these commandments with qaḍā marks them as emphatic, binding divine rulings, not predestination, since the commanded actions may or may not occur.
rows.anchor: وافتتحت هذه الأحكام والوصايا بفعل القضاء اهتماما به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An may be explanatory because qaḍā implies speech, or a verbal noun governed by an understood preposition.
rows.anchor: و ( أن ) يجوز أن تكون تفسيرية لما في ( قضى ) من معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legislation begins with monotheism as the foundation for the following rules and for reform of thought.
rows.anchor: وابتدىء هذا التشريع بذكر أصل التشريعة كلها وهو توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural prohibition addresses everyone and indirectly challenges polytheists; Rabbaka most likely addresses the Prophet, though it may be general.
rows.anchor: وجيء بخطاب الجماعة في قوله : ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command begins with exclusive worship because sound thought must precede sound action; the hadith’s heart parable illustrates this priority.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يشاق العقل إلى طلب الصالحات إلا إذا كان صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥsānan is an absolute object replacing its verb, meaning do good to parents.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { إحسانا } على المفعولية المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-wālidayn is governed by iḥsānan, with bāʾ making it transitive; the phrase is fronted for emphasis and includes each addressee’s parents.
rows.anchor: والباء فيه للتعدية يقال : أحسن بفلان كما يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship belongs to God as creator; parents, as the visible means of human existence and recipients of innate compassion, merit kindness rather than worship.
rows.anchor: فالخالق مستحق العبادة لغناه عن الإحسان ، ولأنها أعظم الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness to parents covers every fitting word, deed, gift, and act of support.
rows.anchor: وشمل الإحسان كل ما يصدق فيه هذا الجنس من الأقوال والأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immā combines the conditional in with extra mā preparing for the emphatic nūn; its spelling reflects assimilation in pronunciation.
rows.anchor: و { إما } مركبة من ( إن ) الشرطية و ( ما ) الزائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The case is one or both parents reaching old age while in the child’s care, when the child must be gentle and accommodating.
rows.anchor: أي إن يبلغ أحد الوالدين أو كلاهما حد الكبر وهما عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is generic, not directed to Muhammad, who then had no parents; singular wording fits the subset of people who have parents.
rows.anchor: وليس خطابا للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ لم يكن له أبوان يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Old age is singled out because caring for parents becomes burdensome and their conduct may be difficult, making kindness more likely to lapse.
rows.anchor: وخص هذه الحالة بالبيان لأنها مظنة انتفاء الإحسان بما يلقى الولد من أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning one parent and both separately makes clear that each arrangement creates distinct excuses for neglect, yet the same duty applies in either case.
rows.anchor: ولم يستغن بإحدى الحالتين عن الأخرى لأن لكل حالة بواعث على التفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The full prohibition against even saying uff is the response to either conditional case.
rows.anchor: فكانت جملة { فلا تقل لهما أف } بتمامها جوابا ل ( إما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic nūn in the condition strengthens its connection to the result.
rows.anchor: وأكد فعل الشرط بنون التوكيد لتحقيق الربط بين مضمون الجواب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most reciters read yablughanna with one parent as the overt subject, so the verb needs no subject marker.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { إما يبلغن } على أن { أحدهما } فاعل

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: They read the dual yablughāni, with the parents as subject and ahaduhumā aw kilāhumā apposed to the dual pronoun to distribute the ruling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف { يبلغان } بألف التثنية ونون مشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address at indaka is generic to every hearer, as confirmed by the preceding and following collective address.
rows.anchor: والخطاب ب { عندك } لكل من يصلح لسماع الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in mercy stands for your mercy, and min marks its source: humility born of compassion, not fear or flattery.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { الرحمة } عوض عن المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aim is to cultivate compassion until it becomes a character trait, as expressed in the cited maxim.
rows.anchor: والمقصود اعتياد النفس على التخلق بالرحمة باستحضار وجوب معاملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duties apply even when parents are polytheists, but children must not obey them in sin or disbelief.
rows.anchor: وهذه أحكام عامة في الوالدين وإن كانا مشركين ، ولا يطاعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports equal dutiful treatment of both parents; when their incompatible requests cannot both be met, one should seek to honor both if possible.
rows.anchor: ومقتضى الآية التسوية بين الوالدين في البر وإرضاؤهما معا في ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A man asked the Prophet who most deserved good companionship; he answered the mother three times, then the father, favoring the mother.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح عن أبي هريرة : أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الليث بن سعد والمحاسبي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: These scholars prefer the mother over the father in filial kindness; Ibn ʿĀshūr reads Mālik’s reported ruling as favoring the mother’s right.
rows.anchor: أحدها : ترجيح الأم على الأب وإلى هذا ذهب الليث بن سعد

rows.speaker: الشافعية
rows.claim: The Shāfiʿīs hold that both parents are equal in the duty of kindness, requiring preference when their requests conflict.
rows.anchor: الثاني : قول الشافعية أن الأبوين سواء في البر

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports al-Muḥāsibī’s view that the mother receives three quarters of filial kindness and the father one quarter.
rows.anchor: وحكى القرطبي عن المحاسبي في كتاب ( الرعاية ) أنه قال : لا خلاف بين العلماء

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports al-Layth’s view that the mother receives two thirds and the father one third, based on variants of the hadith.
rows.anchor: وحكى القرطبي عن الليث أن للأم ثلثي البر وللأب الثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects fixed fractions as unmeasurable and reads both hadith variants as showing a general precedence for the mother.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن تحديد ذلك بالمقدار حوالة على ما لا ينضبط وأن محمل الحديث مع اختلاف روايتيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God for mercy that a child cannot directly bestow on the parents.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر بالدعاء لهما برحمة الله إياهما وهي الرحمة التي لا يستطيع الولد إيصالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The move from the child’s compassion to God’s mercy is a rhetorical transition that encourages seeking the parents’ good in visible and hidden matters, even after death.
rows.anchor: وهذا قد انتقل إليه انتقالا بديعا من قوله : { واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says a person’s deeds end at death except for ongoing charity, useful knowledge, and a righteous child’s prayer for good.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث ( إذا مات ابن آدم انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث : صدقة جارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to pray for parents implies acceptance, and the hadith counts the child’s prayer as a good deed for them; this prayer is restricted to believing parents.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إيماء إلى أن الدعاء لهما مستجاب لأن الله أذن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in kamā rabayānī is a figurative comparison with a causal sense, as in the cited Qur’anic example: ask for matching mercy.
rows.anchor: والكاف في قوله : كما ربياني صغيرا } للتشبيه المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaghīran is a circumstantial accusative describing the speaker’s first-person pronoun.
rows.anchor: وصغيرا } حال من ياء المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of childhood recalls parental compassion: upbringing completes life and mercy protects it, so prayer for mercy expresses gratitude for both.
rows.anchor: فإن الأبوة تقتضي رحمة الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This conclusion addresses differing responses to the parental duty before and after revelation, from compliance to deliberate or inadvertent failure.
rows.anchor: تذييل لآية الأمر بالإحسان بالوالدين وما فصل به ، وما يقتضيه الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the command depends on sincere intention, God knows hearts and promises forgiveness to a child who fulfills the parental duty completely; ṣāliḥīn means those who obey.
rows.anchor: فلذلك ذيله بأنه المطلع على النفوس والنوايا ، فوعد الولد بالمغفرة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun shifts to plural because the statement concerns everyone.
rows.anchor: وغير أسلوب الضمير فعاد إلى ضمير جمع المخاطبين لأن هذا يشترك فيه الناس كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awwābīn broadens the promise to those returning to God; the wording implies that the righteous receive favor and returners receive forgiveness.
rows.anchor: والتقدير إن تكونوا صالحين أوابين إلى الله فإنه كان للصالحين محسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return to God may be constant or follow lapse; both steady obedience and repeated repentance make a person an awwāb, with the intensive form fitting frequency or strength.
rows.anchor: وهذا الأوب يكون مطردا ، ويكون معرضا للتقصير والتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge of the inner self includes lapses and first impulses toward disobedience, showing divine mercy.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم } ما يشمل جميع أحوال النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legal aim is to preserve communal wealth as strength and standing, preventing dependence that others could exploit or dominate.
rows.anchor: والمقصد الشرعي أن تكون أموال الأمة عدة لها وقوة لابتناء أساس مجدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls communal resources your wealth even when held for the incompetent, since they sustain the community until owners become responsible.
rows.anchor: ولهذا أضاف الله تعالى الأموال إلى ضمير المخاطبين في قوله : ولا تؤتوا السفهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction on an incompetent person’s spending aims to prevent waste, but a sound and prudent transaction from that person is valid.
rows.anchor: وما منع السفهاء من التصرف في أموالهم إلا خشية التبذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the prohibition as the verbal noun tabdhīran intensifies it and evokes the whole category of waste and its harms.
rows.anchor: وذكر المفعول المطلق تبذيرا } بعد { ولا تبذر } لتأكيد النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that wasters are brothers of devils explains the forceful prohibition.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين } تعليل للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic article in al-mubadhdhirīn marks a recognized class, as in the wording about the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { المبذرين } تعريف الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression ikhwan means a constant companion; the cited phrase of ʿAdī ibn Zayd calls a Hatra ruler brother of the city because he was associated with it.
rows.anchor: وأخو الحضر إذ بناه وإذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasters are followers and allies of devils, as close as brothers who follow one another.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم من أتباع الشياطين وحلفائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waste serves Satan whether it funds wrongdoing or squanders wealth on trivial pleasures that would otherwise support good works.
rows.anchor: أن التبذير يدعو إليه الشيطان لأنه إما إنفاق في الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waste can become a settled habit; one or two acts can earn the label waster, so an omitted consequence is understood.
rows.anchor: فإذا بذر المرء لم يلبث أن يصير من المبذرين ، أي المعروفين بهذا الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith warns that a person who keeps lying is eventually recorded with God as a liar, illustrating how a repeated vice becomes character.
rows.anchor: كما ورد في الحديث ( إن المرء لا يزال يكذب حتى يكتب عند الله كذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added warning that Satan is ungrateful predicts that waste may lead gradually to disbelief by adopting satanic traits.
rows.anchor: وهذا تحذير شديد من أن يفضي التبذير بصاحبه إلى الكفر تدريجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kufr here can mean ingratitude for wealth; squandering it disobeys God, and habitual waste can lead to habitual ingratitude.
rows.anchor: ويجوز حمل الكفر هنا على كفر النعمة فيكون أقرب درجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy, the waster is ungrateful in outcome or by a nearby degree because wasters are Satan’s companions and Satan is ungrateful.
rows.anchor: إذ كان المبذر مؤاخيا للشيطان وكان الشيطان كفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since pre-Islamic Arabs prized destructive spending and gambling, the verse warns Muslims against unbelieving habits and teaches wise conduct.
rows.anchor: وقد كان التبذير من خلق أهل الجاهلية ، ولذلك يتمدحون بصفة المتلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This instruction continues the duty to give in 17:26; its generic address is aimed especially at Muhammad, who would turn away in embarrassment when unable to give, and also teaches the community.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله : { وآت ذا القربى والمسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAraḍa literally means to turn one’s side; here it figuratively means withholding a gift or avoiding petitioners from shame, as in 17:83.
rows.anchor: والإعراض : أصله ضد الإقبال مشتق من العرض بضم العين أي الجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysūr derives from ease and means gentle, pleasant, acceptable speech; the speaker should apologize kindly and promise help when able.
rows.anchor: والميسور : مفعول من اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away is permitted only from lack of means while seeking God’s provision, not from stinginess, and must be accompanied by kind speech.
rows.anchor: وقد شرط الإعراض بشرطين : أن يكون إعراضا لابتغاء رزق من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking mercy from God marks a truthful explanation of need rather than a pretext.
rows.anchor: وعلم من قوله : ابتغاء رحمة من ربك } أنه اعتذار صادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balanced-spending rule resumes the treatment of waste and stinginess after the intervening verse; conjunction gives it independent emphasis and adds miserliness as the opposite extreme.
rows.anchor: عود إلى بيان التبذير والشح ، فالجملة عطف على جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The virtue is moderate spending between stinginess and profligacy: each extreme harms giver and recipients, while justice puts wealth in proper uses.
rows.anchor: أن المحمود في العطاء هو الوسط الواقع بين طرفي الإفراط والتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording pictures stinginess as a hand chained to the neck and generosity as an extended hand, a familiar rhetorical image.
rows.anchor: وأما البلاغة فبتمثيل الشح والإمساك بغل اليد إلى العنق ، وهو تمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses hands as images of giving: one hand is useful and the other gives even when money is held back.
rows.anchor: يداك يدا صدق فكف مفيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqdir is the opposite of yabsuṭ, a distinction Ibn ʿĀshūr had discussed at 13:26.
rows.anchor: ويقدر } ضد { يبسط } . وقد تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportions provision because He knows servants’ natures and circumstances and what suits each within the divinely ordered world.
rows.anchor: أي هو يفعل ذلك لأنه عليم بأحوال عباده وما يليق بكل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabīr means knowing reports and baṣīr knowing visible things; both names describe aspects of divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: والخبير : العالم بالأخبار . والبصير :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the seventh injunction following 17:23, aimed at a practice rooted in despair of provision; the plural address rejects a common pre-Islamic sin.
rows.anchor: عطف جملة حكم على جملة حكم للنهي عن فعل ينشأ عن اليأس من رزق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast with 6:151 distinguishes killing daughters amid present poverty from killing them out of fear that poverty may arrive later.
rows.anchor: الأول : } أنه قيل هنا { خشية إملاق } وقيل في آية الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Future fear could concern a daughter left poor when her father dies, since pre-Islamic custom denied daughters inheritance; Isḥāq ibn Khalaf’s poem depicts this fear.
rows.anchor: إذا تذكرت بنتي حين تندبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both forms of poverty prompt infanticide; women’s pledge forbade killing children, and Arabs called burying daughters an honor.
rows.anchor: وقد كان ذلك في جملة ما تؤخذ عليه بيعة النساء المؤمنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of them before you contrasts with 6:151, which names parents first because that verse addresses present parental poverty.
rows.anchor: قيل هنالك { نحن نرزقكم وإياهم } بتقديم ضمير الآباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the feared poverty is often the daughters’ future poverty, so God promises provision for children before parents; this is a Qur’anic subtlety.
rows.anchor: وأما الإملاق المحكي في هذه الآية فهو الإملاق المخشي وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imlāq means poverty; Ibn ʿĀshūr had discussed infanticide when commenting on 6:137.
rows.anchor: والإملاق : الافتقار . وتقدم الكلام على الوأد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that their killing is a great sin reinforces the prohibition, and kāna emphasizes its established character.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن قتلهم كان خطأ كبيرا } تأكيد للنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The children meant are specifically girls, but awlād includes daughters; the pronoun follows the word’s grammatical form.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأولاد خصوص البنات لأنهن اللاتي كانوا يقتلونهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiṭʾ with kasra and sukūn means intentional sin; khaṭaʾ with two fatḥas means accidental error, a distinction upheld by Arabic specialists.
rows.anchor: وأما الخطأ بفتح الخاء والطاء فهو ضد العمد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most reciters read khiṭʾ, meaning a deliberate sin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور خطأ } بكسر الخاء وسكون الطاء بعدها همزة

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: They read khaṭaʾ, meaning error opposed to right, with no excuse for the killing.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر { خطأ } بفتح الخاء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads khiṭāʾ, an intensive verbal form for committing sin and a dialect variant of khiṭʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير { خطاء } بكسر الخاء وفتح الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna and kāna emphasize that killing daughters is truly and permanently sinful, rebutting the pre-Islamic claim that burying girls was sound judgment.
rows.anchor: وأكد ب ( إن ) لتحقيقه ردا على أهل الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zina prohibition follows infanticide because fear of dishonor could excuse killing neglected daughters, and illicit sex also wastes lineage.
rows.anchor: عطف هذا النهي على النهي عن وأد البنات إيماء إلى أنهم كانوا يعدون من أعذارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address reflects a practice common among pre-Islamic Arabs; this is the eighth injunction after 17:23.
rows.anchor: وجرى الإضمار فيه بصيغة الجمع كما جرى في قوله : { ولا تقتلوا أولادكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach is a euphemism using the least degree of involvement to express an especially strict prohibition.
rows.anchor: والقرب المنهي عنه هو أقل الملابسة ، وهو كناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic usage defines zina as intercourse outside marriage or an eligible owned-slave relationship; pre-Islamic usage classified intercourse with a free woman and slave prostitution differently.
rows.anchor: والزنى في اصطلاح الإسلام مجامعة الرجل امرأة غير زوجة له ولا مملوكة غير ذات الزوج . وفي الجاهية الزنى : مجامعة الرجل امرأة حرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna, fāḥishah, and kāna intensify the reason for prohibition and depict indecency as a settled quality regardless of prior recognition.
rows.anchor: وجملة إنه كان فاحشة } تعليل للنهي عن ملابسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʾa sabīlan condemns zina; the path is a metaphor for a habitual act built on the metaphor of conduct as walking.
rows.anchor: والسبيل : الطريق . وهو مستعار هنا للفعل الذي يلازمه المرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zina destroys lineage and social care, harms spouses and guardians, exposes women to neglect and divorce, and can spark jealousy, disorder, and killing.
rows.anchor: وعناية الإسلام بتحريم الزنى لأن فيه إضاعة النسب وتعريض النسل للإهمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s line evokes jealous people secretly seeking his death, illustrating the violence that can arise from sexual jealousy.
rows.anchor: علي حراصا لو يسرون مقتلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zina inherently risks lost lineage and violent conflict, so its prohibition is strict both as a goal and as a means; reflection reveals its harms and leaves no excuse after revelation.
rows.anchor: فالزنى مئنة لإضاعة الأنساب ومظنة للتقاتل والتهارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that this verse is Medinan: the claim has no basis, as he argued at the surah’s beginning.
rows.anchor: وقد زعم بعض المفسرين أن هذه الآية مدنية كما تقدم في صدر السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because pre-Islamic Arabs readily killed, preserving life is a universal foundation of Islamic law and this is its ninth injunction here.
rows.anchor: معلومة حالة العرب في الجاهلية من التسرع إلى قتل النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs here means a person or self, as in the cited verses, though it can also mean the human spirit.
rows.anchor: والنفس هنا الذات كقوله تعالى : { ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl is causing a person’s death by an agent’s action.
rows.anchor: والقتل : الإماتة بفعل فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause omits its object pronoun, meaning whom God made inviolable; it prohibits killing the person, not the person’s existence.
rows.anchor: وقوله : حرم الله } حذف العائد من الصلة إلى الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause treats the ban on killing as already known, either from prior rulings or because reflection on human purpose and widespread law should have made it known.
rows.anchor: ووصفت النفس بالموصول والصلة بمقتضى كون تحريم قتلها مشهورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception allows killing when justice establishes a person’s liability; its general wording is explained by known retaliation rules and later legislation.
rows.anchor: واستثني من عموم النهي القتل المصاحب للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-l-ḥaqq indicates accompaniment; ḥaqq means justice or entitlement, illustrated by a hadith about the due right of the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: فالباء في قوله : بالحق } للمصاحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the ban addresses the whole community, authority to determine lawful grounds for execution belongs to appointed decision makers.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الخطاب بالنهي لجميع الأمة كما دل عليه الفعل في سياق النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Hijra, the right was applied according to tribal custom; Muslims in Mecca could face unjust killing by polytheists, so the victim’s guardian received authority to seek retaliation or blood money.
rows.anchor: وحين كان المسلمون وقت نزول هذه الآية مختلطين في مكة بالمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān is a verbal noun for authority, here referring to the established customary law of retaliation.
rows.anchor: والسلطان : مصدر من السلطة كالغفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian may retaliate, forgive, or accept blood money; this orderly right prevents killing innocent relatives and cycles of vengeance.
rows.anchor: وكونه حقا لولي القتيل يأخذ به أو يعفو أو يأخذ الدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation for the killer falls under lawful killing; singled out amid prevalent violence, it begins a just social order instead of reciprocal revenge.
rows.anchor: والقود من جملة المستثنى بقوله : { إلا بالحق } ، لأن القود من القاتل الظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shumaydhir al-Ḥārithī contrasts Islam’s submission to just judgment with a pre-Islamic practice of answering violence by the sword.
rows.anchor: فلسنا كمن كنتم تصيبون سلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarf means exceeding what justice permits, not only financial excess; in killing it includes killing anyone besides the actual killer.
rows.anchor: والسرف : الزيادة على ما يقتضيه الحق ، وليس خاصا بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muhalhil’s revenge poem illustrates excess: he threatens the whole Murra clan for each death in Kalīb’s family.
rows.anchor: كل قتيل في كليب غرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabsha’s poem rejects pricing blood by social rank and accepts retaliation even when the killer is not an equal in status.
rows.anchor: فيقتل جبرا بامرىء لم يكن له

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: They read yusrif with second-person address to the guardian, while the majority reads third person referring to him.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف بتاء الخطاب أي خطاب للولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian already has lawful support through retaliation, so he must not exceed it and turn vindication into injustice.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنه كان منصورا } استئناف ، أي أن ولي المقتول كان منصورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna and kāna affirm the established promise of support; someone who exceeds just limits should not expect such support.
rows.anchor: وقد أكد ذلك بحرف التوكيد وبإقحام ( كان ) الدال على أن الخبر مستقر الثبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān can also allude to a future Muslim ruler who will secure rights when the community gains political order, hinting at a lasting state before Muslims held power.
rows.anchor: ومن نكت القرآن وبلاغته وإعجازه الخفي الإتيان بلفظ ( سلطان ) هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This rule concerns interpersonal murder; defensive warfare has separate rulings.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحكم منوط بالقتل الحادث بين الأشخاص وهو قتل العدوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the wrongfully killed is coordinated as a separate account for emphasis, though it could be an independent explanation or partitive apposition.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن جملة ومن قتل مظلوما } معطوفة على جملة { ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is a general relative used as the subject; the predicate begins with fa because this universal relative is treated like a conditional.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) موصولة مبتدأ مراد بها العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grant of authority first reassures the victim’s guardian, preparing him to accept the ensuing prohibition on excess.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا } هو في المعنى مقدمة للخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By implication, the guardian may not execute the accused privately: state judgment prevents mistaken identity, counter-killings, and excess; yusrif refers back to the guardian.
rows.anchor: ومن دلالة الإشارة أن قوله : { فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا } إشارة إلى إبطال تولي ولي المقتول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that the guardian is supported explains why he must stop short of excess; fī describes excess metaphorically as occurring within the sphere of killing.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنه كان منصورا } تعليل للكف عن الإسراف في القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters deemed the ruling suitable only for committed Muslims and therefore dated the verse to Medina; Ibn ʿĀshūr says he has explained its contextual fit.
rows.anchor: ولما رأى بعض المفسرين أن الحكم الذي تضمنته هذه الآية لا يناسب إلا أحوال المسلمين الخالصين استبعد أن تكون الآية نازلة بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfilling measure and weighing justly are the twelfth and thirteenth injunctions in the sequence begun at 17:23, paralleling the ruling in 6:152.
rows.anchor: هذان حكمان هما الثاني عشر والثالث عشر من الوصايا التي قضى الله بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding idhā kiltum makes the command recur whenever a person measures, disallowing any shortfall; this address to Muslims stresses legislation more than 6:152’s rebuke of polytheists.
rows.anchor: وزيادة الظرف في هذه الآية وهو { إذا كلتم } دون ذكر نظيره في آية الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāla names the seller’s active measuring; the buyer is muktāl, in a paired verb pattern like selling and buying, as illustrated by 83:2–3.
rows.anchor: وفعل ( كال ) يدل على أن فاعله مباشر الكيل ، فهو الذي يدفع الشيء المكيل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most reciters pronounce qistās with a ḍamma on qāf; Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf use a kasra, both being dialect forms.
rows.anchor: و القسطاس بضم القاف في قراءة الجمهور

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid is reported in al-Bukhārī as saying that qistās means justice in Roman speech.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري } ( وقال مجاهد : القسطاس : العدل بالرومية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qistās is said to be a Roman loanword formed from qist, justice, and ṭās, a scale pan; Ibn ʿĀshūr suggests qist abbreviates qistās because Roman words often end in s.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو معرب من الرومية مركب من كلمتين قسط ، أي عدل ، وطاس وهو كفة الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original Roman form began with ḍamma; Arabic speakers allowed a kasra because they did not carefully preserve foreign vowels, as the proverb says of foreign words.
rows.anchor: وأصله في الرومية مضموم الحرف الأول وإنما غيره العرب بالكسر على وجه الجواز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qistās can mean justice or a weighing instrument; here the instrument suits precise legislation for Muslims, while the term also implies fairness and differs from 6:152’s al-qisṭ.
rows.anchor: ومعنى العدل والميزان صالحان هنا ، لكن التي في الأنعام جاء فيها { بالقسط }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here bāʾ indicates use of the instrument and also carries the sense of accompaniment.
rows.anchor: فالباء هنا ظاهرة في معنى الاستعانة والآلة ، ومفيدة للملابسة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mustaqīm means straight or balanced; it plainly describes a scale and is an explanatory attribute of justice.
rows.anchor: والمستقيم : السوي ، مشتق من القوام بفتح القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to measuring and weighing; khayr means better than short measure in afterlife reward and even in worldly peace of conscience.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى المذكور وهو الكيل والوزن المستفاد من فعلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl originally means returning something to its origin or consequences; reflection on fair measure and cheating ultimately shows fair measure to be better.
rows.anchor: والتأويل : تفعيل من الأول ، وهو الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cheating yields little profit but earns contempt and divine anger, while honest measure gains regard, God’s pleasure, self-respect, and blessing in wealth.
rows.anchor: لأن التطفيف يعود على المطفف باقتناء جزء قليل من المال
